steps: Spot which of the three you need: gas volume, atom economy, or percentage yield
For gas volume: find moles of the gas (mass over Mr, then the ratio), then multiply by 24 dm³
For atom economy: Mr of desired product over the Mr of ALL products, times 100
For percentage yield: actual mass or volume over theoretical, times 100
method_card.title: Gas Volumes, Atom Economy and Percentage Yield
method_card.content:
Three calculations, each with its own formula.

Gas volume at RTP: one mole of any gas fills 24 dm³, so \(V = \text{moles} \times 24\). For cm³, multiply by 1000.

Atom economy: a property of the balanced equation, \(\frac{M_r\text{ desired}}{M_r\text{ all products}} \times 100\). Use every coefficient, and put ALL products on the bottom.

Percentage yield: a property of the experiment, \(\frac{\text{actual}}{\text{theoretical}} \times 100\).

From a mass, always find moles first: \(\text{moles} = \frac{\text{mass}}{M_r}\).

exam_context.frequency: High. Atom economy and gas volumes are common in the higher-tier chemistry papers

gold.display: 3.25 g of zinc reacts with excess HCl: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. The student collects 960 cm³ of hydrogen at RTP. Calculate the percentage yield. (Ar: Zn = 65)

misconceptions.message: Theoretical volume = 0.05 × 24 = 1.2 dm³ = 1200 cm³. Yield = (960 ÷ 1200) × 100 = 80%. Match the units (dm³ and cm³) before dividing.

gold.hint: Find the theoretical volume, convert to cm³, then divide.

guided_steps.say: Percentage yield = (actual ÷ theoretical) × 100. Find the theoretical volume from the zinc, and mind the cm³ and dm³ units.

guided_steps.pre: The gas was collected in cm³, so convert: 1.2 × 1000 =

guided_steps.hint: Should give back the gas actually collected.
guided_steps.done: 960 cm³, matches what was collected. Yield = 80%.

gold.display: Two routes can produce calcium oxide. Route A: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (Mr: CaO = 56, CO₂ = 44). Route B: Ca(OH)₂ → CaO + H₂O (Mr: CaO = 56, H₂O = 18). Calculate the atom economy for Route B. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

misconceptions.message: Route B products are CaO + H₂O (56 + 18 = 74), so AE = (56 ÷ 74) × 100 = 75.7%. Using Route A's numbers (56 + 44) gives 56%.

gold.hint: Add both products of Route B for the bottom of the fraction.

guided_steps.say: Atom economy for Route B: the desired product is CaO; the products are CaO and H₂O.

guided_steps.hint: Desired over total, times 100, to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.done: 24.3% is lost as water. Route B atom economy = 75.7%.

gold.display: 32 g of iron(III) oxide reacts with carbon monoxide: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. Calculate the volume of CO₂ produced at RTP. (Mr: Fe₂O₃ = 160)

misconceptions.message: 1 Fe₂O₃ makes 3 CO₂, so moles CO₂ = 0.2 × 3 = 0.6 and V = 14.4 dm³. Forgetting the ×3 ratio gives 4.8 dm³.

gold.hint: Use the 1 to 3 ratio for CO₂, then times 24.

guided_steps.say: Gas volume from a mass: moles, then the ratio, then \(V = \text{moles} \times 24\).

guided_steps.hint: Dividing by 24 should give the moles of CO₂ back.
guided_steps.done: 0.6 mol of CO₂, matches. Volume = 14.4 dm³.

gold.display: 12.25 g of potassium chlorate decomposes: 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂. Calculate the volume of oxygen produced at RTP. (Ar: K = 39, Cl = 35.5, O = 16)

misconceptions.message: 2 KClO₃ make 3 O₂, so moles O₂ = 0.1 × 3 ÷ 2 = 0.15 and V = 3.6 dm³. Ignoring the ratio gives 2.4 dm³.

gold.hint: Find Mr, then moles, then the 2 to 3 ratio, then times 24.

guided_steps.say: Find Mr of KClO₃, then moles, then the 2 : 3 ratio, then \(V = \text{moles} \times 24\).

guided_steps.hint: Add K, Cl and three oxygens.

guided_steps.pre: 2 KClO₃ make 3 O₂, so moles of O₂ = 0.1 × 3 ÷ 2 =

gold.display: 2.5 g of CaCO₃ reacts with excess HCl: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. The student collects 504 cm³ of CO₂ at RTP. Calculate the percentage yield. (Mr: CaCO₃ = 100)

misconceptions.message: Theoretical volume = 0.025 × 24 = 0.6 dm³ = 600 cm³. Yield = (504 ÷ 600) × 100 = 84%. Convert dm³ to cm³ before dividing.

gold.hint: Theoretical volume in cm³, then divide the 504 by it.

guided_steps.say: Percentage yield: theoretical volume of CO₂ from the CaCO₃, then compare with the 504 cm³ collected. Mind the cm³ and dm³ units.

guided_steps.hint: Should give back the CO₂ actually collected.
guided_steps.done: 504 cm³, matches. Yield = 84%.

gold.display: In the decomposition 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂, the desired product is oxygen. Calculate the atom economy. (Ar: K = 39, Cl = 35.5, O = 16)

misconceptions.message: There are 2 KCl (Mr 149) and 3 O₂ (Mr 96), total 245, so AE = (96 ÷ 245) × 100 = 39.2%. Counting only one KCl (74.5) gives 56.3%.

gold.hint: Multiply each product by its coefficient, then divide 3O₂ by the total.

guided_steps.say: Atom economy for oxygen: the desired product is 3O₂; the products are 2KCl and 3O₂. Use the coefficients.

guided_steps.hint: Desired over total, times 100, to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.done: 60.8% is the KCl. Oxygen atom economy = 39.2%.

guided_steps.hint: The molar volume of any gas at RTP.

guided_steps.done: 0.5 mol, back to the start. Volume = 12 dm³.

misconceptions.message: Moles = volume ÷ 24 = 4.8 ÷ 24 = 0.2 mol. Multiplying by 24 instead gives 115.2, which is not a sensible number of moles.

guided_steps.pre: Write the molar volume at RTP: 1 mole =

guided_steps.hint: Multiplying the moles by 24 should give the volume back.

bronze.display: Calculate the volume of 2 mol of oxygen gas at RTP in dm³.

misconceptions.message: Volume = moles × 24 = 2 × 24 = 48 dm³. Dividing gives about 0.08, far too small.

bronze.display: In the reaction CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂, the only desired product is CaO. Calculate the atom economy. (Mr: CaO = 56, CO₂ = 44)

misconceptions.message: Use the Mr of ALL products on the bottom: 56 + 44 = 100, so atom economy = (56 ÷ 100) × 100 = 56%. Putting only CaO on the bottom gives 100%, which would mean no waste.

bronze.hint: Add up the Mr of every product for the bottom of the fraction.

guided_steps.say: Atom economy = (Mr of the desired product ÷ Mr of ALL products) × 100.

guided_steps.pre: Add the Mr of all products: 56 + 44 =

guided_steps.hint: Desired Mr over the total, times 100.

guided_steps.done: 44% is lost as CO₂. Atom economy = 56%.

bronze.display: In the reaction 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, the desired product is MgO. Calculate the atom economy.

misconceptions.message: There is only one product, MgO, so every atom ends up in it. Atom economy = 100%.

bronze.hint: With only one product, all the atoms end up where you want them.

guided_steps.say: Atom economy = (Mr desired ÷ Mr all products) × 100. Count the products of 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.

guided_steps.pre: How many different products are there?
With one product the desired Mr is the whole total, so atom economy = (1 ÷ 1) × 100 =
guided_steps.hint: Every atom ends up in the product you want.

guided_steps.done: No atoms wasted. Atom economy = 100%.

bronze.display: A student expected to make 10 g of a salt but only obtained 7.5 g. Calculate the percentage yield.

misconceptions.message: Percentage yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100 = 7.5 ÷ 10 × 100 = 75%. Dividing the wrong way (10 ÷ 7.5) gives 133%, which is impossible.

bronze.hint: Divide the actual mass by the theoretical mass, then times 100.

guided_steps.say: Percentage yield = (actual ÷ theoretical) × 100.

guided_steps.pre: Which is the theoretical maximum? Write it:
guided_steps.hint: The amount you expected to make.
Should give back the actual mass collected.
guided_steps.done: 7.5 g, matches. Yield = 75%.

steps: Spot which of the three you need. Gas volume: \(V = \text{moles} \times 24\) (dm³ at RTP). Atom economy: \(\frac{M_r\text{ desired}}{M_r\text{ all products}} \times 100\). Percentage yield: \(\frac{\text{actual}}{\text{theoretical}} \times 100\).

steps: Now you get a mass, not moles. Convert first: \(\text{moles} = \frac{\text{mass}}{M_r}\).
Use the equation's ratio to get moles of the gas or product you want, then \(V = \text{moles} \times 24\), or its mass with \(\text{mass} = \text{moles} \times M_r\).
Substitute back and check the value fits.

gold.title: Gold: chain two steps or convert units
steps: Gold questions combine skills. For percentage yield from a gas, find the theoretical amount first (mass, moles, ratio, volume), then compare with what was collected.
Watch the units: if the gas is in cm³ but the molar volume gives dm³, convert with \(1\text{ dm}^3 = 1000\text{ cm}^3\) before dividing.
For atom economy, use every coefficient: \(2\text{Fe}\) means \(2 \times M_r\), then \(\frac{M_r\text{ desired}}{M_r\text{ all products}} \times 100\).
